subject.title: fix(update): dev channel update builds from an unverified checkout at the git install path

question: Should package-to-dev switching continue adopting arbitrary preexisting OpenClaw-shaped checkouts, or must it use only a checkout created and owned by OpenClaw?
rationale: Remote verification cannot close the execution and transport trust boundary, while removing adoption changes an existing contributor-oriented workflow; repository policy requires an explicit owner choice rather than a partial denylist.

options.title: Require managed checkout
options.body: Refuse preexisting unmanaged directories and clone the canonical repository into an empty, OpenClaw-owned path while preserving in-place updates for installations already running from a checkout.

options.title: Keep partial remote guard
options.body: Land the URL check as limited accidental-fork protection while explicitly accepting residual arbitrary-code execution and the new fork-layout incompatibility.

options.title: Pause the dev switch path
options.body: Temporarily stop package installations from switching to a Git-backed dev channel until a managed-checkout lifecycle is designed and proven.

recommendation.title: Require managed checkout
recommendation.body: Refuse preexisting unmanaged directories and clone the canonical repository into an empty, OpenClaw-owned path while preserving in-place updates for installations already running from a checkout.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent update/runtime history makes steipete the strongest available owner for deciding the permanent package-to-Git trust boundary.
